title: A complementary dataset of open-eyes EEG recordings in a photo-stimulation setting from: Alzheimer's disease, Frontotemporal dementia and Healthy subjects
description: This dataset provides complementary EEG recordings, obtained under photic stimulation with eyes open, from a cohort of individuals with Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia, and healthy controls previously described in a related open-eyes-closed EEG dataset. Recordings were collected at incremental photic stimulation frequencies (5-30 Hz) at the 2nd Department of Neurology, AHEPA University Hospital, Thessaloniki, Greece, using a 19-channel clinical EEG system. The dataset includes both raw and preprocessed (denoised) EEG data, intended to support research on neurodegenerative disease biomarkers and cognitive decline.
methods_description: EEG recordings were acquired using a Nihon Kohden EEG 2100 clinical device with 19 scalp electrodes (10-20 system) plus 2 mastoid electrodes, sampled at 500 Hz. Participants were seated with eyes open while exposed to photic stimulation at incremental frequencies from 5 Hz up to 30 Hz. Preprocessing included a 0.5-45 Hz Butterworth band-pass filter, re-referencing to A1-A2, Artifact Subspace Reconstruction (ASR) for artifact correction, and Independent Component Analysis (ICA) with automatic classification (ICLabel) to remove eye and jaw artifact components.
